card.title: Galaxy XCover 6 Pro Backlight Not Working

source.title: Galaxy XCover 6 Pro Backlight Not Working

claims.statement: XCover 6 Pro backlight output LED_A_24P runs from coil L9001 (10 µH) through diode D9000, smoothing caps, then L9032 to the display.
A burnt open L9001 is rarely the root cause; check D9000 (should read one way only) and the six smoothing caps C9004, C9005, C9020, C9021, C9030, C9031 for shorts to ground.
An iPad 5 backlight diode can substitute for D9000; a same-size backlight coil from another Samsung LCD model can replace L9001.
The backlight circuit sits under a large shield on the back near the SIM flex; cutting the shield is safer than lifting it because the CPU is directly opposite.
Find a shorted cap by injecting about 1 V at 2–3 A and watching a thermal camera or freeze spray.

procedure: Test a known-good screen and inspect the display FPC connector.
Cut open the shield over the backlight circuit.
Check L9001 continuity; replace if open.
Diode-test D9000 both directions; replace if equal both ways.
Diode-check C9004/C9005/C9020/C9021/C9030/C9031 to ground; inject 1 V to find the short and remove it.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Lifting the whole shield with hot air risks floating the CPU on the other side.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
